newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jailed for mad cow disease extortion bid.
newsitem.headline: German jailed for mad cow disease extortion bid.

text.p: A German who tried to extort millions of marks from Swiss Nestle's Maggi unit by threatening to inject its food products with mad cow disease was jailed for three years and two months on Friday.
The man, identified as Rainer M., said heavy debts led him to seek to extort money from the company earlier this year.
A court in the southern town of Konstanz handed his wife, Gabriele M., a one-year suspended sentence for her part in the crime.
Mad cow disease, known scientifically as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), is a fatal cattle brain disease which can produce a human equivalent blamed for several human deaths.
The sentence comes as German police investigated a new extortion attempt on Thomy, a sister company of Maggi within the multinational Nestle food group.
It received a letter earlier this week claiming that its products in stores around the country had been contaminated.

Police said on Friday they had completed their examinations of products pulled from the shelves in all the supermarkets which could have been targeted by the extortionist and had found no trace of any contamination.
The threat, which was made public on Tuesday evening, sparked a nationwide alert. More than 15,000 people flooded police with phone calls on an emergency number.
Authorities have appealed to members of the public to return mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, coffee, cocoa, tea and chocolate bought since August 1 bearing the Thomy or Nestle brand names.
